title: Quotient Gauss norm and Banach topology of a Tate quotient
statement:
Let $K$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. Write $T_r=K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_rangle$ for the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with Gauss norm $\|\sum_
u a_

u\|_G=\sup_
u|a_
u|$, where coefficients tend to zero. Let $C
e0$ be a commutative unital Banach $K$-algebra with nonarchimedean submultiplicative norm $\|\cdot\|_C$ satisfying $\|ac\|_C=|a|\|c\|_C$, and let $q:T_r	o C$ be a continuous surjective $K$-algebra homomorphism. Then $\|c\|_q=\inf\{\|f\|_G:q(f)=c\}$ is a complete nonarchimedean submultiplicative $K$-algebra norm, induces the quotient topology, and is equivalent to $\|\cdot\|_C$: there are positive real constants $A,B$ with $\|c\|_q\le A\|c\|_C$ and $\|c\|_C\le B\|c\|_q$ for all $c\in C$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] with $F=K$ and $n=r$. It gives a complete Gauss-normed ring $T_r$ with ultrametric triangle inequality, $\|1\|_G=1$ and $\|fg\|_G\le\|f\|_G\|g\|_G$. The coefficient formula gives $\|af\|_G=|a|\|f\|_G$ for $a\ne0$ by taking the supremum after multiplying every coefficient value by $|a|>0$; for $a=0$ both sides vanish. Thus $T_r$ is a Banach $K$-vector space. The assumptions make $C$ a Banach $K$-vector space too, and the given algebra homomorphism $q$ is a continuous surjective linear map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-continuous-linear-map-norm-bound] to $q$ to get $B>0$ with $\|q(f)\|_C\le B\|f\|_G$ for every $f$. Apply [lem-trf-banach-surjective-bounded-lifts] to the same map between the Banach spaces of step 1 to get $A>0$ such that every $c$ has a lift $f$ with $\|f\|_G\le A\|c\|_C$. Both results apply over the same nontrivially normed field $K$; the second result uses completeness of both spaces, already checked. No finite-dimensionality or discrete valuation is used.

proof.text: For each $c$, the set $S_c=\{\|f\|_G:q(f)=c\}$ is nonempty by surjectivity and bounded below by zero. Put $N(c)=\inf S_c$. It is finite and nonnegative, and for every $\epsilon>0$ there is a lift of $c$ with norm less than $N(c)+\epsilon$: otherwise that larger number would be a lower bound for $S_c$. For every lift of $c$, step 2 gives $\|c\|_C/B\le\|f\|_G$. Taking the infimum gives $\|c\|_C\le B N(c)$. Its bounded lift gives $N(c)\le A\|c\|_C$. Since zero lifts zero, $N(0)=0$; the first inequality implies $N(c)=0$ only for $c=0$.

proof.text: Negation bijects lifts of $c$ and $-c$ without changing their Gauss norms, so $N(-c)=N(c)$. For $a\ne0$, multiplication by $a$ bijects lifts of $c$ and $ac$, scaling their norms by $|a|$; consequently $N(ac)=|a|N(c)$ by the defining greatest-lower-bound property. For $a=0$ the identity follows from $N(0)=0$. Given $\epsilon>0$, take lifts $f,g$ of $c,d$ with norms less than $N(c)+\epsilon,N(d)+\epsilon$. Their sum lifts $c+d$, so the Gauss ultrametric bound of step 1 gives $N(c+d)\le\max(N(c),N(d))+\epsilon$. Letting $\epsilon$ decrease to zero gives the ultrametric inequality for $N$.

proof.text: For the same approximate lifts, $fg$ lifts $cd$ and step 1 gives $N(cd)\le(N(c)+\epsilon)(N(d)+\epsilon)$. Let $\epsilon$ decrease to zero to obtain $N(cd)\le N(c)N(d)$. The lift $1\in T_r$ gives $N(1)\le1$. Since $C\ne0$, definiteness implies $N(1)>0$; submultiplicativity applied to $1=1\cdot1$ gives $N(1)\le N(1)^2$, hence $N(1)\ge1$. Thus $N(1)=1$, and scalar homogeneity also gives $N(a1)=|a|$. These calculations establish all algebra-norm axioms without requiring any infimum to be attained.

proof.text: For $t>0$ one has $q(\{f:\|f\|_G<t\})=\{c:N(c)<t\}$. One inclusion follows from $N(q(f))\le\|f\|_G$; for the other, choose $0<\epsilon<t-N(c)$ in step 3. Translation gives the same equality for balls centered at any $f_0$ and $q(f_0)$. Therefore $q$ is open for the $N$-topology, since balls form a basis, and it is continuous by $N(q(f)-q(g))\le\|f-g\|_G$. A surjective continuous open map induces the quotient topology: if $q^{-1}(U)$ is open then $U=q(q^{-1}(U))$ is open, and the converse is continuity.

source.place: Section 1.4, Proposition 4(i)–(ii), printed p.23; alternative Banach open mapping route following Proposition 19, printed p.31. Agent proof using the cited Mathlib and DAG statements; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The two inequalities in step 3 applied to differences show that the $N$ and original $C$ norm topologies coincide (each ball contains an appropriately scaled ball for the other norm). They also prove completeness directly: an $N$-Cauchy sequence is Cauchy for $\|\cdot\|_C$ by $\|c-d\|_C\le BN(c-d)$; it has a limit $c$ in the given Banach algebra, and $N(c_n-c)\le A\|c_n-c\|_C\to0$. Thus the $N$ metric is complete. Together with steps 3–6 this proves the stated equivalence, quotient topology and complete nonarchimedean submultiplicative algebra norm.
